extracted.intended_audience: comedy writers, playwrights, screenwriters, and dramatists studying mistaken-identity mechanics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating or evaluating comedy built on mistaken identity (Comedy of Errors mechanism): how to structure confusion, sustain dramatic irony, escalate beats, and deliver a satisfying revelation payoff. Useful for plays, sitcom episodes, and farce where identity confusion is the central engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural identity confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there structural identity confusion? Unlike comedies of disguise (where someone deliberately deceives), Comedy of Errors humor occurs when nobody pretends to be anyone else, yet confusion still ensues. Identity confusion is structural, not deceptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the confusion arises from circumstance or coincidence (e.g., separated identicals, lookalikes), not from deliberate impersonation. The mechanism should make identical or interchangeable identities plausibly available so misidentification can drive scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience knows more than the characters (dramatic irony)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the audience know more than the characters? Audience knows truth; characters don't. Dramatic irony saturates every interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the audience slightly ahead of the characters so they can anticipate collisions and enjoy the characters' bumbling. Use staging, exposition, or parallel scenes to reveal the truth to the audience while withholding it from most characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistakes compound through the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do mistakes compound through the work? Each new misunderstanding compounds the previous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a chain-reaction structure where one misread or misidentification leads directly to further errors. Avoid isolated gags that don't affect subsequent scenes; aim for a snowball effect that raises stakes and confusion over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each beat escalates confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Is each new beat an escalation of confusion? Each character's actions, while internally rational, produce escalating chaos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make individual beats logically defensible for the characters but ensure their consequences increase disorder. Each interaction should raise the comic tension rather than reset it—use misunderstandings to amplify misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revelation must pay off the buildup
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the eventual revelation pay off the buildup? The final unmasking/resolution should resolve the compounded mistakes satisfactorily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the revelation so it answers the central confusions and provides emotional/comic catharsis. The payoff should feel earned by the chain of prior beats rather than arbitrary; tie loose ends to earlier clues or misreadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twin confusion (practical engine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Twin Confusion: identical twins separated and reunited (Antipholi, Dromios). Each interaction with a twin produces wrong outcomes; one twin gets beaten while the other receives affection meant for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use twin or lookalike pairs to create parallel scenes where characters consistently mistake one for the other. Exploit physical similarities, shared names/titles, and split entrances/exits to maximize mismatches and reciprocal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double meanings / contextual misinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Double Meanings: statements interpreted by the hearer in the wrong context. Speakers don't know they're being misread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write lines with semantic ambiguity or rely on context shifts so that ordinary statements take on wrong meanings. Puns and equivocation can fuel misunderstandings, but avoid relying solely on wordplay—contextual mismatch should affect actions and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cascading misunderstanding (design pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cascading Misunderstanding: one mistake leads to more mistakes in a snowball effect; eventually only revelation can stop the escalation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the plot as interlocking mistakes rather than isolated incidents. Each error should create conditions for the next—use misdelivered messages, missed meetings, and false assumptions to build an inexorable chain toward a culminating confusion that the revelation will resolve.
